BiblicalUsage: Rabak is to soak bread or cake in oil — the meat offering baked in a pan: 'In a pan it shall be made with oil; and when it is baken, thou shalt bring it in.' The Chronicler counts the Levites' charge over the fine flour and the oil and the cakes mingled with oil.
TheologicalSignificance: What this says to me is that even the oil-soaked cake matters: God prescribed the details of worship, and the Levites kept them, because He is worthy of care in small things.
